algorithms.name: Slowly Moving Bandit (SMB) applied to an HST tree approximating the metric

symbols.C_c: covering complexity of the metric, sup_{0<eps<1} eps * N^c_eps(Delta)

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: Let $(K,\dist)$ be a finite metric space over $\abs{K} = k$ elements with diameter $\le 1$ and \upper $\dimu = \dimu(\dist)$. There exists an algorithm such that for any sequence of loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T$ guarantees that $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\dist) = \tO\Lr{ \max\Lrset{ \dimu^{1/3} T^{2/3}, \sqrt{kT} } }$.

results.notes: Movement regret includes the movement costs. Algorithm: SMB on a dominating HST tree (Lemma 14 + Lemma 13); efficient per the paper. Tree construction depends on T.

symbols.C_p: packing complexity of the metric, sup_{0<eps<1} eps * N^p_eps(Delta)

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Let $(K,\dist)$ be a finite metric space over $\abs{K} = k$ elements with diameter $\ge 1$ and \low $\diml = \diml(\dist)$. For any algorithm there exists a sequence $\ell_1,\ldots, \ell_{T}$ of loss functions such that $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\dist) = \wt{\Omega}\Lr{ \max\Lrset{ \diml^{1/3} T^{2/3}, \sqrt{kT} } }$.

results.notes: Proof is a sketch reducing to Dekel et al. 2014 on a packing.

symbols.d_M: upper Minkowski dimension of the metric space

source.label: thm:coverdim
source.quote: Let $(K,\dist)$ be a metric space with diameter $\le 1$ and upper Minkowski dimension $d = \cdim(\dist)$, such that $d\ge 1$. There exists a strategy such that for any sequence of loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T$, which are all $1$-Lipschitz with respect to $\dist$, guarantees that $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\dist) = \tO\Lr{ T^\frac{d+1}{d+2} }$.

results.notes: Via discretization to a 2eps-cover and Theorem 7. Hidden constant depends on the metric.

symbols.C_T: complexity of the HST metric (covering = packing complexity)

conditions: metric is an HST metric induced by a 2-HST tree with leaves at the same depth H

source.label: lem:smb-tree
source.quote: Let $(K,\distT)$ be a metric space defined by a $2$-HST $\cT$ with $\depth(\cT) = H$ and \upperlow $\dim(\cT)=\dim$. Using SMB algorithm we can achieve the following regret bound: $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\distT) = \O\LR{ H \sqrt{2^H T \dim \smash{\log\dim }} + H 2^{-H} T }$

results.notes: H here is tree depth, not episode length. Same bound appears as the tuned statement of Theorem 16.

conditions: metric is an HST metric induced by a tree of depth H

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Assume that the metric $\dist = \distT$ is a metric specified by a tree $\cT$ which is a HST with $\depth(\cT) = H$ and \upperlow $\dim(\cT)=\dim$. Then, for any sequence of loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots, \ell_T$, \cref{alg:smb} guarantees that $\mregret(\ell_{1:t},\distT) = \O\LR{ \frac{H\log{\dim}}{\eta} + \eta \dim H 2^H T + H 2^{-H} T }$.

results.notes: Tuned version of this theorem equals Theorem 11 (r4); not duplicated.

conditions: metric is an HST tree metric satisfying conditions (1) and (2a or 2b) of Corollary 12 (well-behaved depth relative to T)

source.label: cor:smb-goodtree
source.quote: Let $(K,\distT)$ be a metric space defined by a tree $\cT$ over $\abs{K}=k$ leaves with $\depth(\cT)=H$ and \upperlow $\dim(\cT)=\dim$. Assume that $\cT$ satisfies the following: (1) $ 2^{-H} H T\le \sqrt{2^H H \dim T}$; (2) One of the following is true: (a) $2^{H}\dim \le k$; (b) $ 2^{-(H-1)} (H-1) T\ge \sqrt{2^{H-1} (H-1) \dim T}$. Then, the SMB algorithm can be used to attain ...

results.notes: Conditions in appendix restatement differ slightly from main text.

conditions: metric is any HST tree metric

source.label: lem:tree
source.quote: For any tree $\cT$ and time horizon $T$, there exists a tree $\cT'$ ... that satisfies the conditions of \cref{cor:smb-goodtree}, such that $\dist_{\cT'} \ge \dist_{\cT}$ and $\dim(\cT') = \dim(\cT)$. ... Hence, applying SMB to the metric space $(K,\dist_{\cT'})$ leads to $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\distT) = \tO\Lr{ \max\Lrset{\dim(\cT)^{1/3} T^{2/3}, \sqrt{kT}} }$.

results.notes: Special case of Theorem 7 for tree metrics.
